rounds.text: Rajapalayam Mills Ltd carries severe fundamental and balance sheet risks that undermine its seemingly cheap headline valuation [E1, E2]. Despite a low price-to-book ratio of 0.31x and a P/E of 6.69, the company generates an abysmal return on capital employed of just 1.8% and a median return on equity of only 5% over 10 years, dropping to 2% over the last 3 years [E1, E2, E6, E20, E22]. Operational efficiency is further undermined by a low interest coverage ratio, stagnant long-term profit growth of only 1% over 10 years, and persistent share price destruction resulting in a 5-year compounded share price growth of -7% [E12, E17, E54]. Leverage is substantial with borrowings climbing to Rs 1,146 Cr in March 2026, accompanied by massive contingent liabilities of Rs 363 Cr and a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.58x where profits outpace actual operating cash flow [E28, E33, E56]. Institutional confidence is practically non-existent, evidenced by domestic institutions slashing their holdings from 0.36% to 0.02%, while technical indicators show the stock trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside an extreme annualised volatility of 270.5% [E37, E44, E47]. Conceded: [E39] A discounted cash flow model estimates an intrinsic value of Rs 1568 per share and the market value of investments exceeds the market capitalisation [E53].
